text.tspan: The spirit of it. The details live in docs/ and scripts/; dig there when you need them.
a test fails: back to the repo that owns it
red on dev: fix in that repo, redeploy
Always on, outside the lanes: every pull request in every repo runs its own CI
lint, types, unit tests, and a check that the repo still speaks the agreed API. No AWS. A PR that changes the API is refused there and sent to /ship.
Pick the code: each repo at its PR branch, the others at the last known-good version
Build the images that do not exist yet
Update AWS: Terraform for the infrastructure, Helm for the apps
Run the tests through the public URL, as a browser would
Post the verdict, and exactly which versions ran, on the PR
Inside step 4, when the dbt models change
Helm first runs the release job: rebuild the data, publish the new metric definitions
The indexer re-embeds the metrics, so questions can find them
Only then does the gateway switch to the new release, with no downtime
Separately, every night: refresh the searchable values (states, categories...)
make login, then make push-gh-creds: lends CI a
short-lived AWS session. GitHub keeps no keys.
make dev-up starts dev from the known-good
versions (~25 min). make dev-down stops it.
Not built yet: release-prod.yml is a
placeholder until a prod environment exists.
